messages.subject: checking for NA in Rcpp
parts:
I know this sounds stupid but how do I check if a value in a vector is NA from within a cpp function?

Consider the following very simple function:
// [[Rcpp::export]]
void f(IntegerVector v)
{
    int n = v.size();
    for(int i=0; i<n; i++)
    {
        if(R_IsNA(v[i])) {
            printf("v[%d] is NA\n", i);
        } else {
            printf("v[%d] is NOT NA\n", i);
        }
    }
}

If I do:
>v=integer(3);
>v[1]=NA;
>f(v);
I get that all of them are NOT NA
I know there is a synthetic suger function is_na but it fails to compile if I replace R_IsNA with it (probably because it returns a vector, i.e. I would have to allocate a vector of the same size, which will get TRUE/FALSE but that is not my goal,
I simply want to test if a specific element is NA before I do calculations on it.
Any ideas?

messages.subject: Re: checking for NA in Rcpp
parts:
this is sort of answering my own questions but still.
I have no idea why R_IsNA doesn't work (it should according to everything I found) but as a work around I found I could use:
IntegerVector::is_na(v[i])
and
NumericVector::is_na(v[i])
